title: 361. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Area of Trapezoids and Parallelograms
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area of a parallelogram using its base and height.
questions.question: A parallelogram has base \(7\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\text{ cm}\). What is its area?
questions.explanation:
Use the parallelogram area formula \(A=bh\). Substitute \(b=7\text{ cm}\) and \(h=4\text{ cm}\):
\(A=7\times 4=28\).
So the area is \(28\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: For a parallelogram, area equals base times the corresponding height.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area of a trapezoid from its two parallel sides and height.
questions.question: A trapezoid has parallel sides \(6\text{ cm}\) and \(10\text{ cm}\), and height \(5\text{ cm}\). What is its area?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h\). Substitute \(b_1=6\), \(b_2=10\), and \(h=5\):
\(A=\frac{1}{2}(6+10)\times 5=\frac{1}{2}\times 16\times 5=40\).
Therefore, the area is \(40\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Add the two parallel sides first, then use the trapezoid area formula.

questions.concept: Height of a Parallelogram from Area
questions.learningObjective: Determine the height of a parallelogram from its area and base.
questions.question: A parallelogram has area \(72\text{ cm}^2\) and base \(9\text{ cm}\). What is its height?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=bh\). Substitute \(A=72\) and \(b=9\):
\(72=9h\).
Divide both sides by \(9\):
\(h=8\).
So the height is \(8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Rearrange \(A=bh\) to solve for the height.

questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown parallel side of a trapezoid from its area and height.
questions.question: A trapezoid has area \(54\text{ cm}^2\), height \(6\text{ cm}\), and one parallel side \(8\text{ cm}\). What is the length of the other parallel side?
questions.explanation:
Use \(A=\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h\). Let the unknown side be \(x\text{ cm}\). Substitute the known values:
\(54=\frac{1}{2}(8+x)\times 6\).
Simplify:
\(54=3(8+x)\).
Divide by \(3\):
\(18=8+x\).
Thus, \(x=10\). The other parallel side is \(10\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Substitute the known values into the trapezoid area formula, then solve for the unknown base.

questions.concept: Area of a Parallelogram with Unit Conversion
questions.learningObjective: Calculate parallelogram area after converting measurements to the same unit.
questions.question: A parallelogram has base \(1.5\text{ m}\) and height \(40\text{ cm}\). What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.explanation:
Convert the base to centimeters:
\(1.5\text{ m}=150\text{ cm}\).
Then use \(A=bh\):
\(A=150\times 40=6000\).
So the area is \(6000\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Convert both measurements to the same unit before multiplying.

questions.concept: Area of a Trapezoid with Decimal Measurements
questions.learningObjective: Calculate trapezoid area using decimal side lengths and height.
questions.question: A trapezoid has parallel sides \(2.4\text{ m}\) and \(1.6\text{ m}\), and height \(0.5\text{ m}\). What is its area?
questions.explanation:
Add the parallel sides:
\(2.4+1.6=4.0\text{ m}\).
Then use \(A=\frac{1}{2}(b_1+b_2)h\):
\(A=\frac{1}{2}\times 4.0\times 0.5=1.0\).
Therefore, the area is \(1\text{ m}^2\).
questions.hint: Find the sum of the parallel sides first, then multiply by half the height.

questions.concept: Effect of Changing Base and Height on Parallelogram Area
questions.learningObjective: Analyze how changing base and height affects the area of a parallelogram.
questions.question: The base of a parallelogram is doubled, and its height is halved. What happens to its area?
questions.explanation:
Let the original base be \(b\) and original height be \(h\). The original area is \(bh\). After the changes, the new base is \(2b\) and the new height is \(\frac{h}{2}\). The new area is
\(2b\times \frac{h}{2}=bh\).
So the area remains unchanged.
questions.hint: Write the original area as \(bh\), then substitute the new base and new height.

questions.concept: Comparing Areas of a Trapezoid and a Parallelogram
questions.learningObjective: Compare the areas of a trapezoid and a parallelogram using their formulas.
questions.question: A trapezoid has parallel sides \(5\text{ cm}\) and \(7\text{ cm}\), and height \(4\text{ cm}\). A parallelogram has base \(6\text{ cm}\) and height \(4\text{ cm}\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: B
options.text: The trapezoid has the greater area.

questions.explanation:
For the trapezoid:
\(A=\frac{1}{2}(5+7)\times 4=\frac{1}{2}\times 12\times 4=24\).
For the parallelogram:
\(A=6\times 4=24\).
Both areas are \(24\text{ cm}^2\), so they have equal areas.
questions.hint: Calculate each area separately using the correct formula.

questions.concept: Missing Base of a Trapezoid from Area and Height
questions.learningObjective: Solve for the shorter base of a trapezoid when one base is longer by a fixed amount.
questions.question: A trapezoid has area \(60\text{ cm}^2\), height \(6\text{ cm}\), and one parallel side \(4\text{ cm}\) longer than the other. What is the length of the shorter parallel side?
questions.explanation:
Let the shorter side be \(x\text{ cm}\). Then the longer side is \(x+4\text{ cm}\). Use the trapezoid area formula:
\(60=\frac{1}{2}(x+x+4)\times 6\).
Simplify:
\(60=3(2x+4)\).
Divide by \(3\):
\(20=2x+4\).
Then \(2x=16\), so \(x=8\).
The shorter parallel side is \(8\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Let the shorter base be \(x\), express the longer base as \(x+4\), and substitute into the trapezoid area formula.

questions.concept: Equal Areas of a Parallelogram and a Trapezoid
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown trapezoid base by equating its area to a given parallelogram area.
questions.question: A parallelogram has base \(12\text{ cm}\) and height \(5\text{ cm}\). A trapezoid has height \(6\text{ cm}\) and one parallel side \(8\text{ cm}\). If the trapezoid has the same area as the parallelogram, what is the length of its other parallel side?
questions.explanation:
The parallelogram area is
\(12\times 5=60\text{ cm}^2\).
For the trapezoid, let the unknown side be \(x\text{ cm}\). Its area is
\(\frac{1}{2}(8+x)\times 6=3(8+x)\).
Set this equal to \(60\):
\(3(8+x)=60\).
Divide by \(3\):
\(8+x=20\).
Thus, \(x=12\). The other parallel side is \(12\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: First find the parallelogram area, then set the trapezoid area expression equal to that value.
